thread.title: Stock Futures Mixed: Dow Leads, Baidu Dives; VA Deal Lifts Cerner

author: EdJenner
title: Stock Futures Mixed: Dow Leads, Baidu Dives; VA Deal Lifts Cerner
text:
CLOSE Japan, Europe Extend Rallies To Eight Weeks
Friday’s economic calendar is largely empty. Oil prices may see some effect from Baker Hughes ( BHGE ) rig count survey, set for release at 1 p.m. ET. U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude traded a fraction higher early Friday, holding above $71 a barrel and up 0.8% for the week and still pecking away at 42-month highs.
Asian stocks markets shifted higher Friday. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index ticked up 0.3%, leaving it 0.2% lower for the week. The Shanghai Composite surged 1.2%, enough for a 0.9% advance for the week — lifting it back above support at its 50-day moving average in its fourth straight weekly gain. In Japan, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 tacked on a 0.4% gain Friday, taking a 0.8% gain in its eighth straight up week.
Stocks in Europe nursed thin losses at midday, as benchmarks in London, Paris and Frankfurt all tracked toward their eighth straight weekly gain. For the week, the CAC-40 in Paris led, up 1.5%. Baidu, Applied Materials Dive; Deere Edges Up On Guidance; Cerner Inks $10 Billion Deal
Cerner rose more than 7%, leading both the Nasdaq and the S&P 500. The company announced late Thursday it had signed a $10 billion, 10-year contract to provide electronic health records technology to the U.S. Veterans Affairs Department. Cerner is also in the process of rolling out a pilot program at the Pentagon, worth up to $9 billion. Cerner climbed back above support at its 10-week moving average over the past two weeks, but remains 18% below its January high.
Apple ( AAPL ) rose 0.3%, and all of the FANG stock tech leaders traded higher.
Ag and construction equipment maker Deere ( DE ) angled up 0.7%, as strong fiscal third-quarter and full-year sales guidance were tempered by a weak fiscal second-quarter performance. The stock has been attempting to retake support at its 10-week moving average, ending Thursday’s 17% below its mid-February high.
On the Nasdaq 100, Baidu tumbled more than 5% to the bottom of the index. The company announced a management shake-up late Thursday, with Chief Operating Officer Qi Lu stepping down and Haifeng Wang taking over as senior vice president and general manager of Baidu’s AI Group. No successor COO was named. Baidu shares broke out above a 275.07 buy point this week, but in moderate trade. Friday’s premarket loss suggests the stock would open back below its buy point. Not all premarket moves carry over into regular trade.
Applied Materials took a 6% hit, falling after reporting a better-than-forecast 54% EPS gain and 29% rise in revenue for its fiscal second quarter. But Q3 revenue guidance stopped short of consensus estimates. The stock has been bogged down in a consolidation and struggling to maintain support sicne Novemgber, after clearing a late-stage base in September.
